title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates may trigger Remote Desktop failures
content_md: Microsoft has confirmed that non-admin users may be unable to connect to devices via Remote Desktop after installing recent Windows updates if the "Administrator protection" security feature is enabled. This feature began rolling out with the KB5067036 preview cumulative update to systems running Windows 11 24H2/25H2 in October 2025, and it is now enabled by default in organizations using Windows security baselines after installing the October 2026 Windows security update. When toggled on, admin protection ensures logged-in users have only standard user permissions and prompts them to authenticate via Windows Hello (PIN or biometric) when they try to install new apps or change the Windows registry. On Tuesday, Microsoft confirmed that Remote Desktop connections may fail with error 0xC000000D after installing the KB5124010 September 2026 non-security preview update or later updates on systems running Windows 11 24H2/25H2/26H1/26H2. "Attempts to connect might fail with error 0xC000000D and display the message, 'The token that was passed to the function is invalid.' This issue primarily affects enterprise-managed remote devices used as Remote Desktop hosts with Administrator protection enabled, regardless of how the feature was enabled," it said .
